prompt:
Renovate this exact room photograph. Keep the architecture exactly as in the input image: same wall planes, same opening positions and sizes, same ceiling height, same floor level, same camera position, same perspective, same framing and aspect ratio. Do not add, remove, resize or move any opening.

The input photograph shows: Living room, rectangular, deeper than wide, 3.6 m x 4.5 m; ceiling 2.7 m; floor: medium oak wood planks laid lengthwise toward the far wall, continuous single-level floor plane, no steps. Front-left floor-to-ceiling window/sliding door behind curtains 3.2 x 2.4 m, sill 0 m, 50% along the wall. Camera 1.5 m high, 4 m to the far wall, 24 mm lens, tilt -2 degrees, horizon 45% of frame height. The number of openings is exactly 1; do not add or remove any opening. Opening proportion: the opening is nearly wall-to-wall, leaving only narrow piers at each end. Fixed features that stay: skirting board: painted timber skirting along the base of the right wall, approx 80 mm high; wall-mounted air-conditioner: split-type indoor unit high on the right wall near the far corner; electrical distribution box: recessed metal panel high on the right wall; weak-current box: small recessed low-voltage panel lower on the right wall; installed ceiling fittings: flush round ceiling light and a recessed downlight near the curtain wall.

LIGHTING DESIGN
The room is lit by one key light: daylight entering from the front-left opening(s). Every shadow in the room runs away from that wall.
Practical fixtures are decorative only: at most two visible fixtures, warm 2700 K, low output. They do not cast shadows, do not add fill light, and do not glow.
No bloom, no halo, no light spill on the ceiling, no lens flare, no double shadows. The window stays readable, never blown to white.
Interior exposure is balanced for the room, not for the view outside.
Style-specific lighting: a black iron arc floor lamp and a metal pendant are the only practical fixtures, and the daylight reveals velvet nap, cognac leather grain and linen weave.
You may change the lighting completely; the original photo's light is not a constraint.
Keep window openings physically unchanged while changing what comes through them.

FURNISHING AND DECOR
Interior styling, in industrial loft: Raw-shell industrial loft vocabulary: exposed concrete beams, columns and ducts, white painted brick and latex walls, polished micro-cement floors, black steel grid windows casting daylight shadows. Palette anchors warm taupe #967F6B, espresso #3B2C20, bone #E4D4C5, burnt orange #B2441A, iron black #1D1916, olive #5A5041. Mid-century modular velvet sofas, chrome-and-leather lounge chairs, Noguchi glass tables, ceramic stools, track spotlights, arc lamps, jute rugs, checkerboard wool, plaid and knit throws.
Seating: burnt orange modular velvet sofa, chrome framed cognac leather lounge chair, glazed ceramic stool; Table surfaces: Noguchi style glass coffee table, espresso brown writing table with laptop and notebook; Storage/display: low iron and oak shelf unit with visible books, ceramic vessels and brass clock; Textiles: bone cream linen curtains, jute rug, checkerboard wool throw, plaid cushions; Appliances: matte black espresso machine, black electric kettle, slim turntable; Greenery: tall fiddle leaf fig in taupe clay pot, trailing pothos, olive bowl of moss; Wall decor: burnt orange abstract canvas, round iron framed mirror, woven jute wall hanging; Tabletop objects: stacked art books, amber glass vase, ceramic tray with brass keys; Lighting fixtures: black iron arc floor lamp, black metal dome pendant. Furnish the room with a burnt orange modular velvet sofa, a chrome-framed cognac leather lounge chair, a Noguchi-style glass coffee table, a glazed ceramic stool, a black iron arc floor lamp, and a jute rug. Additional requirement: Decorate the living room.
Density target: at least 12 distinct furnishing and decor items, at least 3 styled surfaces, 2 layered textiles per seating area.

Everything in the original room except the architectural shell is replaced: all furniture, soft furnishings, light fittings, textiles, decor and colours are new.

Hard corrections, these override other instructions: Restore the medium oak lengthwise plank floor and the flat 2.7 m ceiling (remove the concrete beam), rebuild the front-left opening as a floor-to-ceiling sliding door filling ~90% of that wall, add the painted timber skirting on the right wall, and turn off the pendant/arc practicals so all shadows run from the single left window.

REALISM
Shot as an editorial interior photograph for a design magazine: 35 mm full-frame body, 24 mm tilt-shift kept level, natural imperfect surfaces - fabric wrinkles, curtain folds that are not perfectly symmetrical, faint scuffs on the skirting, real dust-free but lived-in tabletops, subtle sensor grain, gentle highlight rolloff. No retouching sheen, no HDR, no CGI, no archviz, no perfectly uniform material, no flawless symmetry, no plastic reflections.

Vertical 3:4 composition.
